evidence: Turner’s first *chōkara branch gives Hindi chorā/chorī, Gujarati chorɔ/chorī/chorũ and the addendum’s Kiunthali ċhoru child/boy. These western child/son/daughter and boy/girl forms match that r-family, with regional s/ṣ/ś/ts realization and vowel raising retained. They are kept distinct from the retained-k chokr- branch and the different orphan entry *chōra.

Direct comparanda include Hindi/Punjabi chokrā and Gujarati chokrɔ; the Gujari expanded cokār- forms are qualified regional members. evidence: Turner *laḍikka gives Punjabi laṛkā, western Pahari laṛkā and Kumauni laṛīk alongside Hindi laṛkā/laṛkī. The Jaunsari diminutive -ṭo/ṭu and Hindi feminine expansion are retained. This is a family assignment: Turner himself allows some forms alternatively under the doubled *laḍḍikka branch, so the deeper consonant history is not claimed to be certain.

Turner explicitly lists Hindi ṭābar boy/family and western Pahari ṭabər family member under *ṭabbara. These Kaithal tabar/tēbar child responses fit that specific regional family; the survey’s dental spelling and vowel variant are preserved.
